# Reference spec — Bookmark management application · Level (A) implementable

- Domain: bookmark management
- Common initial prompt: "I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks."
- Reference OSS: Linkding (Sascha Sieber, https://github.com/sissbruecker/linkding)
  — its public README/docs were **referenced** to derive the feature set; this is
  not a reproduction of a specific product but represents the domain's feature ceiling.
- Spec level: **(A)** — entities, behaviour rules, states, edge cases, and
  acceptance conditions, at a level where a **functionally equivalent
  re-implementation is possible** even if the UI/code differ.
- Status: not a comparison arm but the **coverage upper-bound anchor** and the
  client's standardised tacit knowledge. No execution session.
- Coverage unit: **functional requirement (REF-BM-###)**.

---

## 1. Overview / scope

A single-user application to save, categorise, search, and revisit web links
(bookmarks), and to manage read state and archiving. On save it automatically
collects metadata from the remote page; it organises with tags, search, and
bundles, and preserves a snapshot of the original. The scope below splits into
the user features the client co-constructs (core / extended) and the operational
features excluded from the denominator (infra).

## 2. Core entities

| Entity | Fields | Constraints / relations |
|---|---|---|
| Bookmark | url, title, description, note (markdown), unread flag, archived flag, favicon, preview image, snapshot reference, created-at, updated-at | url required. Many-to-many with tags. Re-saving the same url should lead to editing the existing bookmark, not creating a new one. |
| Tag | name | Name unique within the user scope. Many-to-many with bookmarks. |
| Bundle | name, search term, included tags, excluded tags | A saved filter. When viewed, dynamically selects bookmarks matching the conditions. |
| User settings | default sort, displayed items, font size | Personal profile settings. |

## 3. Functional requirements

### 3.1 Core

- REF-BM-01: Save a bookmark by entering a url.
- REF-BM-02: On save, automatically collect the target page's title, description, favicon, and preview image.
- REF-BM-03: The user can edit the auto-collected title/description before and after saving.
- REF-BM-04: Edit a bookmark's url/title/description/tags/note.
- REF-BM-05: Delete a bookmark.
- REF-BM-06: When re-saving an existing url, guide the user to edit the existing bookmark instead of creating a new one.
- REF-BM-07: Display the bookmark list readability-first, exposing title, description, tags, and favicon per item.
- REF-BM-08: Selecting a list item navigates to the original url.
- REF-BM-09: Assign one or more tags to a bookmark.
- REF-BM-10: On tag entry, offer existing tags as autocomplete.
- REF-BM-11: Select a specific tag to filter to only that tag's bookmarks.
- REF-BM-12: Full-text search over title, description, note, and url.
- REF-BM-13: Search is case-insensitive.
- REF-BM-14: Search tags with the `#tag` syntax.
- REF-BM-15: Use AND/OR/NOT operators and parenthesised groups in the search term (e.g. `rome (#article or #book)`). Rule: the operators themselves must be quoted to be treated as literal search terms.
- REF-BM-16: Search a quoted phrase as an exact match.
- REF-BM-17: Mark a bookmark as "read later" (unread).
- REF-BM-18: View only unread bookmarks separately.
- REF-BM-19: Mark a bookmark as read to remove it from the unread list.
- REF-BM-20: Select multiple bookmarks to perform a bulk action (add/remove tags, read/unread, archive, delete).
- REF-BM-21: Apply a bulk action to the whole collection matching the current filter.
- REF-BM-22: Sort the list by a sort key (date added, title, etc.).

### 3.2 Extended

- REF-BM-23: Write a markdown note on a bookmark and render it when viewing.
- REF-BM-24: Preserve a snapshot of the bookmarked page as local HTML (single file). Rule: if the url is a PDF, download and store the PDF instead of an HTML snapshot.
- REF-BM-25: Support creating a snapshot on the Internet Archive.
- REF-BM-26: Archive a bookmark to hide it from the default list/search while keeping its content.
- REF-BM-27: Distinguish archive from delete — archive is reversible, delete is permanent removal.
- REF-BM-28: View only archived bookmarks as a separate list.
- REF-BM-29: Save a combination of search term and included/excluded tags as a bundle for reuse.
- REF-BM-30: Import bookmarks in Netscape HTML format (preserving title, tags, date added).
- REF-BM-31: Export bookmarks in Netscape HTML format.
- REF-BM-32: Adjust display-related personal settings (default sort, displayed items, font size, etc.).

### 3.3 Infra — excluded from the coverage denominator

- REF-BM-I01: Multi-user support and a self-service admin panel.
- REF-BM-I02: SSO (OIDC) / auth-proxy login.
- REF-BM-I03: Third-party integration REST API.
- REF-BM-I04: Browser extensions (Firefox/Chrome) / bookmarklet / PWA share sheet.
- REF-BM-I05: Backup and raw-data access.

## 4. Edge cases / business rules

- Archived bookmarks are excluded from the default list and ordinary search results, and appear only in the archive list.
- In search, tag search (`#`) and full-text search combine with AND, and boolean/parentheses/phrases are supported.
- "Apply to whole collection" for bulk actions is limited to the scope defined by the current filter (search term / tag / perspective).
- A duplicate save attempt of the same url converges to editing the existing item, preventing duplicates.
- If a snapshot target url is a PDF, download and store the PDF instead of an HTML snapshot.

## 5. Coverage scoring convention

- Unit: each `REF-BM-###`. Judge whether the feature a method elicited/implemented realises each item as **present / partial / absent**.
- Direction: one-way (reference -> method). Whether a method produced a feature not in the reference is not judged (no ground truth) and is not measured.
- Denominator: primary = core (3.1); secondary = core + extended (3.1 + 3.2). Infra (3.3) is excluded.
- To mitigate judgment bias, run and report a blind secondary judgment and inter-rater reliability.

## Item counts

- Core (REF-BM-01..22): 22
- Extended (REF-BM-23..32): 10
- Infra (REF-BM-I01..I05): 5

1	# Feature Specification: Bookmark Manager
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `001-bookmark-manager`
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-07-13
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	**Input**: User description: "An app to save and manage bookmarks"
10	
11	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
12	
13	### User Story 1 - Save a bookmark (Priority: P1)
14	
15	A person finds a web page they want to return to later and saves it into the app by
16	providing its address. The app captures the page so it can be found again.
17	
18	**Why this priority**: Saving is the core reason the app exists. Without it there is
19	nothing to manage. This single capability already delivers value — a reliable place to
20	stash links.
21	
22	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by saving a link and confirming it appears in
23	the list of saved bookmarks, delivering the value of "I won't lose this page."
24	
25	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
26	
27	1. **Given** an empty collection, **When** the user saves a valid web address, **Then**
28	   a new bookmark appears in their collection showing at least the address and a title.
29	2. **Given** a web address with no title supplied, **When** the user saves it, **Then**
30	   the app stores it with a sensible fallback title (e.g. the address itself).
31	3. **Given** a malformed or empty address, **When** the user tries to save it, **Then**
32	   the app rejects it with a clear message and saves nothing.
33	
34	---
35	
36	### User Story 2 - Browse and find saved bookmarks (Priority: P1)
37	
38	The user opens the app and sees the bookmarks they have saved, and can quickly locate a
39	specific one among many.
40	
41	**Why this priority**: A collection that cannot be viewed or searched is not
42	manageable. Viewing and finding is inseparable from the core value of saving.
43	
44	**Independent Test**: Can be tested by pre-loading several bookmarks, opening the list,
45	and confirming they are all shown and that searching by a keyword narrows the list.
46	
47	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
48	
49	1. **Given** several saved bookmarks, **When** the user opens the app, **Then** all
50	   bookmarks are listed with their title and address.
51	2. **Given** a collection of bookmarks, **When** the user searches by a word in the
52	   title or address, **Then** only matching bookmarks are shown.
53	3. **Given** no bookmarks saved yet, **When** the user opens the app, **Then** a friendly
54	   empty state explains how to add the first bookmark.
55	
56	---
57	
58	### User Story 3 - Organize bookmarks with tags (Priority: P2)
59	
60	The user assigns one or more labels (tags) to bookmarks and later filters the collection
61	by a tag to see a focused subset.
62	
63	**Why this priority**: Organization becomes valuable once a collection grows. It is
64	important but not required for the app to be useful on day one.
65	
66	**Independent Test**: Can be tested by tagging bookmarks, then filtering by a tag and
67	confirming only bookmarks carrying that tag are shown.
68	
69	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
70	
71	1. **Given** a saved bookmark, **When** the user adds one or more tags to it, **Then**
72	   those tags are stored and displayed with the bookmark.
73	2. **Given** bookmarks with various tags, **When** the user filters by a tag, **Then**
74	   only bookmarks carrying that tag are shown.
75	
76	---
77	
78	### User Story 4 - Edit and delete bookmarks (Priority: P2)
79	
80	The user corrects a bookmark's details or removes bookmarks they no longer need.
81	
82	**Why this priority**: Keeping a collection accurate and uncluttered matters for
83	long-term use, but the app is still usable without it initially.
84	
85	**Independent Test**: Can be tested by editing a bookmark's title and confirming the
86	change persists, and by deleting a bookmark and confirming it disappears from the list.
87

# Feature Specification: Bookmark Manager

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "An app to save and manage bookmarks"

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Save a bookmark (Priority: P1)

A person finds a web page they want to return to later and saves it into the app by
providing its address. The app captures the page so it can be found again.

**Why this priority**: Saving is the core reason the app exists. Without it there is
nothing to manage. This single capability already delivers value — a reliable place to
stash links.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by saving a link and confirming it appears in
the list of saved bookmarks, delivering the value of "I won't lose this page."

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** an empty collection, **When** the user saves a valid web address, **Then**
   a new bookmark appears in their collection showing at least the address and a title.
2. **Given** a web address with no title supplied, **When** the user saves it, **Then**
   the app stores it with a sensible fallback title (e.g. the address itself).
3. **Given** a malformed or empty address, **When** the user tries to save it, **Then**
   the app rejects it with a clear message and saves nothing.

---

### User Story 2 - Browse and find saved bookmarks (Priority: P1)

The user opens the app and sees the bookmarks they have saved, and can quickly locate a
specific one among many.

**Why this priority**: A collection that cannot be viewed or searched is not
manageable. Viewing and finding is inseparable from the core value of saving.

**Independent Test**: Can be tested by pre-loading several bookmarks, opening the list,
and confirming they are all shown and that searching by a keyword narrows the list.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** several saved bookmarks, **When** the user opens the app, **Then** all
   bookmarks are listed with their title and address.
2. **Given** a collection of bookmarks, **When** the user searches by a word in the
   title or address, **Then** only matching bookmarks are shown.
3. **Given** no bookmarks saved yet, **When** the user opens the app, **Then** a friendly
   empty state explains how to add the first bookmark.

---

### User Story 3 - Organize bookmarks with tags (Priority: P2)

The user assigns one or more labels (tags) to bookmarks and later filters the collection
by a tag to see a focused subset.

**Why this priority**: Organization becomes valuable once a collection grows. It is
important but not required for the app to be useful on day one.

**Independent Test**: Can be tested by tagging bookmarks, then filtering by a tag and
confirming only bookmarks carrying that tag are shown.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a saved bookmark, **When** the user adds one or more tags to it, **Then**
   those tags are stored and displayed with the bookmark.
2. **Given** bookmarks with various tags, **When** the user filters by a tag, **Then**
   only bookmarks carrying that tag are shown.

---

### User Story 4 - Edit and delete bookmarks (Priority: P2)

The user corrects a bookmark's details or removes bookmarks they no longer need.

**Why this priority**: Keeping a collection accurate and uncluttered matters for
long-term use, but the app is still usable without it initially.

**Independent Test**: Can be tested by editing a bookmark's title and confirming the
change persists, and by deleting a bookmark and confirming it disappears from the list.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** an existing bookmark, **When** the user edits its title, address, or tags,
   **Then** the updated details are saved and displayed.
2. **Given** an existing bookmark, **When** the user deletes it and confirms, **Then** it
   is removed from the collection and no longer appears.
3. **Given** a delete action, **When** it is triggered, **Then** the user is asked to
   confirm before the bookmark is permanently removed.

---

### Edge Cases

- What happens when the user saves an address that is already bookmarked? The app warns
  of the duplicate and lets the user keep the existing entry rather than silently
  creating a second copy.
- How does the system handle a very long title or address? It stores the full value and
  displays it in a way that does not break the layout (e.g. truncated with full value
  available).
- What happens when a search or tag filter matches nothing? The app shows a clear "no
  matching bookmarks" state rather than an empty screen.
- How does the system behave when the user has a large number of bookmarks? The list
  remains responsive and usable (see Success Criteria).
- What happens if the user enters an address without a scheme (e.g. "example.com")? The
  app normalizes it to a valid web address before saving.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: System MUST allow a user to save a bookmark by providing a web address.
- **FR-002**: System MUST allow a user to optionally provide a title when saving; when
  none is given, the system MUST supply a fallback title derived from the address.
- **FR-003**: System MUST validate that a submitted address is a well-formed web address
  and reject invalid input with a clear message, saving nothing.
- **FR-004**: System MUST persist saved bookmarks so they remain available across
  sessions.
- **FR-005**: System MUST display the user's saved bookmarks in a list showing at least
  title and address.
- **FR-006**: Users MUST be able to search bookmarks by keywords matching the title or
  address, with the list narrowing to matches.
- **FR-007**: System MUST present a clear empty state when no bookmarks exist and a clear
  "no results" state when a search or filter matches nothing.
- **FR-008**: Users MUST be able to assign zero or more tags to a bookmark and to remove
  tags.
- **FR-009**: Users MUST be able to filter the collection by a tag to see only bookmarks
  carrying that tag.
- **FR-010**: Users MUST be able to edit an existing bookmark's title, address, and tags,
  with changes persisted.
- **FR-011**: Users MUST be able to delete a bookmark, with a confirmation step before
  permanent removal.
- **FR-012**: System MUST detect when a user saves an address that already exists and warn
  of the duplicate rather than silently storing a second copy.
- **FR-013**: System MUST record when each bookmark was saved so the collection can be
  presented in a meaningful order (most recent first by default).

### Key Entities *(include if feature involves data)*

- **Bookmark**: A saved reference to a web page. Key attributes: web address, title,
  optional description/note, the tags applied to it, and the date/time it was saved.
- **Tag**: A short user-defined label used to group bookmarks. A tag may apply to many
  bookmarks, and a bookmark may carry many tags.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: A user can save a new bookmark in under 15 seconds from opening the add
  action to seeing it in the list.
- **SC-002**: A user can locate a specific bookmark in a collection of at least 500
  entries within 10 seconds using search or tag filtering.
- **SC-003**: 95% of first-time users successfully save and later retrieve a bookmark
  without external guidance.
- **SC-004**: Search and filter results appear to the user as immediate (perceived within
  1 second) for collections up to 1,000 bookmarks.
- **SC-005**: No saved bookmark is lost between sessions — 100% of saved bookmarks are
  present when the user returns.

## Assumptions

- This is a single-user personal app for the first version; multi-user accounts,
  sharing, and collaboration are out of scope for v1.
- User authentication is out of scope for v1; the collection belongs to the local user of
  the app.
- Bookmarks reference web addresses (http/https); other schemes are out of scope for v1.
- Automatic fetching of page metadata (title, favicon, preview) beyond a simple fallback
  title is a potential enhancement, not required for v1.
- Import/export of bookmarks (e.g. from a browser) is out of scope for v1.
- The app targets standard modern usage expectations for responsiveness and reliability;
  specific platform (web, desktop, mobile) is deferred to the planning phase.

Thanks — this is a good start and I can tell you've thought about it. Reading it over, though, a fair bit of what I picture is either missing or not quite how I'd want it. Let me go through it.

**On your scope questions:**

1. A couple of those boundaries I'd actually want pulled *into* v1:
   - **Auto-grabbing the page info.** When I save a link, I really don't want to type the title myself. I'd expect the app to go look at the page and fill in its title and description for me automatically — and ideally grab the little site icon and a preview image too. I should still be able to tweak what it grabbed, before or after saving. A plain "fallback title from the address" isn't enough for me.
   - **Import and export.** I've got piles of bookmarks already, and I'd hate to lose them if I ever move. So I want to be able to bring in a bookmarks file (the kind browsers give you) and also export mine back out.
   - Multi-device sync I'm fine leaving out for now, and web-links-only is fine.

2. On the duplicate thing — you said it "warns and lets me keep the existing entry." What I'd actually want is: if I save a link I've already got, it just takes me to the one I already saved so I can edit it. Not a second copy, not really a warning to dismiss — just quietly send me to the existing one.

**On fields:** yes, beyond address/title/description/tags/date, I'd want a **notes** area where I can jot my own longer thoughts (and I'd like that to keep basic formatting like headings and lists). And when I'm typing a tag, please **suggest tags I've already used** so I don't end up with "recipe" and "recipes."

**On missing stories — several things I expected aren't here:**

- **Opening a bookmark.** Clicking one in the list should take me to the actual web page. That's the whole point.
- **A "read later" pile.** I want to mark things as unread/to-read and be able to look at just those, then mark them done so they drop off that list.
- **Archiving, separate from deleting.** Sometimes I'm done with a link but don't want to throw it away. I'd want to tuck it away so it's out of my main list and searches, but still there if I go looking — as opposed to delete, which is gone for good.
- **Keeping a copy of the page.** Pages disappear over time. I'd love the app to save a snapshot of the page as it was when I bookmarked it, so I can still read it later even if the original vanishes.
- **Smarter searching.** Searching just title and address feels thin. I'd want it to search my notes and the address too, ignore capitalization, let me search by tag, and let me combine terms — like "find things tagged recipe *or* tagged dinner" or search an exact phrase.
- **Sorting and picking a lot at once.** I'd want to sort the list different ways (newest, by title), and to select a bunch of bookmarks and do one thing to all of them — tag them, archive them, delete them together.

Could you fold these in and let me have another look before we move on?

319	  and tags, ignoring capitalization.
320	- **FR-014**: Users MUST be able to filter or search by tag.
321	- **FR-015**: Users MUST be able to combine search terms (including OR across tags and requiring
322	  multiple terms together) and to search for an exact phrase.
323	- **FR-016**: System MUST exclude archived bookmarks from default searches unless the user is
324	  searching within the archive.
325	
326	**Tags**
327	
328	- **FR-017**: Users MUST be able to assign zero or more tags to a bookmark and remove tags.

330	  to encourage reuse and avoid near-duplicate tags.
331	
332	**Editing, notes & deletion**
333	
334	- **FR-019**: Users MUST be able to edit an existing bookmark's title, address, description, and
335	  tags, with changes persisted.
336	- **FR-020**: Users MUST be able to write personal notes on a bookmark using basic rich
337	  formatting (such as headings and lists), and the formatting MUST be preserved.
338	- **FR-021**: Users MUST be able to delete a bookmark permanently, with a confirmation step
339	  before removal.
340	
341	**Read-later**
342	
343	- **FR-022**: Users MUST be able to mark a bookmark as to-read (unread) and as read/done.
344	- **FR-023**: System MUST provide a read-later view showing only to-read bookmarks, and a
345	  bookmark marked read MUST drop off that view while remaining in the collection.
346	
347	**Archiving**
348	
349	- **FR-024**: Users MUST be able to archive a bookmark, removing it from the main list and
350	  default searches while preserving it in an archive.
351	- **FR-025**: Users MUST be able to view archived bookmarks and unarchive them to return them to
352	  the main list. Archiving MUST be distinct from and never perform a permanent delete.
353

357	  at save time.

359	  page is unavailable; when a snapshot could not be captured, System MUST indicate it is
360	  unavailable without blocking the save.
361	
362	**Bulk actions**
363	
364	- **FR-028**: Users MUST be able to select multiple bookmarks at once.
365	- **FR-029**: Users MUST be able to apply a single action — add a tag, archive, or delete — to
366	  all selected bookmarks at once, with destructive bulk actions requiring confirmation.
367	
368	**Import & export**
369	
370	- **FR-030**: Users MUST be able to import bookmarks from a standard browser bookmarks file,
371	  adding the entries to their collection using the same dedupe rule as manual saving.
372	- **FR-031**: System MUST reject a malformed or unsupported import file with a clear message,
373	  importing nothing.
374	- **FR-032**: Users MUST be able to export their collection to a file.
375	
376	### Key Entities *(include if feature involves data)*
377	
378	- **Bookmark**: A saved reference to a web page. Attributes: web address, title, short
379	  description, personal notes (rich text), site icon, preview image, the tags applied to it,
380	  read state (to-read / read), archived state, date/time saved, and a reference to its snapshot.
381	- **Tag**: A short user-defined label used to group bookmarks. A tag may apply to many
382	  bookmarks, and a bookmark may carry many tags.
383	- **Snapshot**: A stored copy of a page's readable content captured at the time a bookmark was
384	  saved, linked to that bookmark, and viewable even if the original page later changes or
385	  disappears.
386	
387	## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
388	
389	### Measurable Outcomes
390	
391	- **SC-001**: A user can save a new bookmark in under 15 seconds without typing any page
392	  details, and the fetched title/description/icon/preview appear on the bookmark within a few
393	  seconds without blocking further use of the app.
394	- **SC-002**: A user can locate a specific bookmark in a collection of at least 500 entries
395	  within 10 seconds using search, tag filtering, or sorting.
396	- **SC-003**: 95% of first-time users successfully save, find, and open a bookmark without
397	  external guidance.
398	- **SC-004**: Search, filter, and sort results appear to the user as immediate (perceived within
399	  1 second) for collections up to 1,000 bookmarks.
400	- **SC-005**: No saved bookmark is lost between sessions — 100% of saved (and archived)
401	  bookmarks are present when the user returns.
402	- **SC-006**: A user can import a browser bookmarks file of at least 500 entries and see them in
403	  their collection, with no duplicates created for addresses they already had.
404	- **SC-007**: A user can open a saved snapshot and read the page's content even when the original
405	  page is unreachable, for 100% of bookmarks whose snapshot was captured.
406	
407	## Assumptions
408	
409	- This is a single-user personal app for the first version; multi-user accounts, sharing, and
410	  collaboration are out of scope for v1.
411	- User authentication is out of scope for v1; the collection belongs to the local user.
412	- **Multi-device sync is out of scope for v1** (confirmed with client).
413	- Bookmarks reference web addresses (http/https); other schemes are out of scope for v1.
414	- Automatic page-detail fetching, page snapshots, and import/export are **in scope for v1**
415	  (pulled in during client review).
416	- "Basic rich formatting" for notes means a small, common set such as headings, bold/italic, and
417	  lists — not a full document editor.
418	- Snapshots capture the page's readable content; perfectly faithful reproduction of every page
419	  (complex scripts, media, paywalled content) is not guaranteed.
420	- Import targets the standard bookmarks file format that browsers export; format-specific edge
421	  cases beyond that are out of scope for v1.
422	- The specific platform (web, desktop, mobile) is deferred to the planning phase.
